Read-only exploration of /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Do NOT modify anything. Do NOT run any build/test/lint command — I only want you to READ configuration and docs to inventory what gates exist.

GOAL: Produce a complete inventory of this repo's deterministic quality gates, so I can run them myself and record baseline numbers.

Search breadth: medium-thorough.

Cover:
1. Every script in root `package.json`'s "scripts" block — name, exact command, and one line on what it does. Pay special attention to: test, lint, build, typecheck-ish (tsc), audit:tokens, test:max-file-size, test:story, env, and anything storybook/playwright/vitest related.
2. `.github/workflows/qa.yml` (at current HEAD of the `develop`-merged tree, i.e. the working copy) — enumerate every job, what command each job runs, and every `if:` condition that can cause a job to skip or no-op.
3. `vitest.config.ts` — does it set `passWithNoTests`? What `include`/`exclude` patterns? What does a "0 tests" run look like?
4. `.storybook/` test runner config and `playwright.config.*` — how are tests discovered, what would make them match zero files.
5. `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — its exit-code behaviour and whether it is documented as having known pre-existing violations.
6. `.husky/` and `scripts/hooks/` — what pre-commit/commit-msg/pre-push enforce.

7. CRITICALLY: search `.docs/`, `.claude/rules/`, and script header comments for any statement that a gate currently FAILS or has KNOWN PRE-EXISTING violations at baseline (e.g. phrases like "pre-existing", "not wired into CI", "14 violations", "known failures", "not gated"). I need to know in advance which gates exit non-zero on a healthy tree, because a non-zero exit code there is NOT a PR failure.

REPORT FORMAT: a table of Gate | exact command | what a PASS looks like as an ITEM COUNT (not exit code) | known baseline noise/known-failing. Then a short list of "gates that can silently pass having run zero items" with the specific mechanism. Cite file:line for each claim. Be concise — no code dumps.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session.      7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.

    17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
    18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
    19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
    20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21	
    22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
    24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
    25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

    27	  # fnm

    29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
    30	  fi
    31	
    32	  # volta
    33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
    35	  fi
    36	
    37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    40	    exit 1
    41	  fi
    42	fi
    43	
    44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
    46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48	
    49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
    50	
    51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
    52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
    53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
    54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
    55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
    56	
    57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
    58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
    59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
    60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
    61	  git add .claude/registry/
    62	fi
    63	
    64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
    66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
    67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
    68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
    69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    70	
    71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
    72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    74	    || true)
    75	
    76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."

    79	      echo ""
    80	      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
    81	      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
    82	      echo ""
    83	      exit 1
    84	    fi
    85	    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
    86	  fi
    87	fi
    88	
    89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    90	# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
    91	#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
    92	#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
    93	#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
    94	#     automatically.
    95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    97	skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    98	  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
    99	  || true)

   102	  echo ""
   103	  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
   104	  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

   106	  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then

   109	    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
   110	  fi
   111	
   112	  echo ""
   113	  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
   114	  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
   115	  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
   116	  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
   117	  echo ""
   118	fi
   119	
   120	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   121	# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
   122	#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
   123	#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
   124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125	
   126	experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
   127	  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
   128	  || true)
   129	
   130	if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
   131	  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."
   132	
   133	  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
   134	  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
   135	  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT
   136	
   137	  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
   138	  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
   139	  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
   140	  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
   141	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   142	    name=$(basename "$f")

   145	      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"

   147	      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
   148	    fi
   149	  done

   151	  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
   152	    echo ""
   153	    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."

   160	fi

   162	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   163	# 3. Derived configuration file guard
   164	#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
   165	#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
   166	#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
   167	#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
   168	#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
   169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   170	
   171	blocked_files=()
   172	
   173	# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
   174	modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)
   175	
   176	while IFS= read -r file; do
   177	  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
   178	
   179	  # Only check files in derived locations
   180	  case "$file" in
   181	    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
   182	    *) continue ;;
   183	  esac
   184	
   185	  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
   186	  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
   187	  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
   188	  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue
   189	
   190	  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
   191	  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
   192	  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
   193	    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
   194	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')
   195	
   196	  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue
   197	
   198	  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
   199	  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
   200	  # Skip it.
   201	  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
   202	  any_source_staged=false
   203	  while IFS= read -r src; do
   204	    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
   205	    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
   206	    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
   207	      any_source_staged=true
   208	      break
   209	    fi
   210	  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
   211	  if $any_source_staged; then
   212	    continue
   213	  fi
   214	
   215	  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
   216	  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
   217	  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
   218	  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
   219	  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
   220	  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
   221	  # not a direct edit.
   222	  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
   223	    continue
   224	  fi
   225	
   226	  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
   227	  blocked_files+=("$file")
   228	
   229	done <<< "$modified_staged"
   230	
   231	if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   232	  echo ""
   233	  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
   234	  echo ""
   235	  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
   236	    echo "       $bf"
   237	  done
   238	  echo ""
   239	  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
   240	  echo ""
   241	  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
   242	  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
   243	  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
   244	  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
   245	  echo ""
   246	  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
   247	  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
   248	  echo ""
   249	  exit 1
   250	fi
   251	
   252	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   253	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
   254	#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
   255	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
   256	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
   257	#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
   258	#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
   259	#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
   260	#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
   261	#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
   262	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   263	
   264	if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
   265	  secret_violations=()
   266	
   267	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   268	    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
   269	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
   270	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
   271	    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
   272	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   273	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
   274	
   275	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
   276	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
   277	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
   278	      continue
   279	    fi
   280	
   281	    # Value looks like a JWT
   282	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
   283	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
   284	      continue
   285	    fi
   286	
   287	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
   288	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
   289	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
   290	      continue
   291	    fi
   292	
   293	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
   294	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
   295	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
   296	      continue
   297	    fi
   298	
   299	    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
   300	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
   301	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
   302	      continue
   303	    fi
   304	
   305	  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)
   306	
   307	  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   308	    echo ""
   309	    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
   310	    echo ""
   311	    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
   312	      echo "    $v"
   313	    done
   314	    echo ""
   315	    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
   316	    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."

   318	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."

   322	fi

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
     3	#
     4	# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
     5	# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
     6	# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
     7	# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
     8	#
     9	# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
    10	#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
    11	#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
    12	# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
    13	#
    14	# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
    15	#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
    16	# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
    17	# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
    18	# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
    19	# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
    20	rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
    21	final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
    22	status=0
    23	
    24	while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
    25	  case "$remote_ref" in
    26	    refs/tags/v*)
    27	      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
    28	      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
    29	        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
    30	        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
    31	        status=1
    32	      fi
    33	      ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done
    36	
    37	exit $status

   209	    fi

   213	  fi

   217	  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
   218	  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
   219	  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
   220	  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,

   253	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard

   255	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
   256	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.

   262	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   265	  secret_violations=()
   266

   269	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
   270	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue

   272	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   273	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

   275	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
   276	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then

   279	    fi
   280	
   281	    # Value looks like a JWT
   282	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
   283	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
   284	      continue
   285	    fi
   286	
   287	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
   288	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then

   291	    fi
   292	
   293	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
   294	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
   295	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")

   302	      continue
   303	    fi
   304	
   305	  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

   308	    echo ""
   309	    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
   310	    echo ""
   311	    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
   312	      echo "    $v"
   313	    done
   314	    echo ""
   315	    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
   316	    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
   317	    echo ""
   318	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
   319	    echo ""
   320	    exit 1

   322	fi

     2	# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
     3	#
     4	# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
     5	# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
     6	# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
     7	# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
     8	#
     9	# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
    10	#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
    11	#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
    12	# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
    13	#
    14	# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
    15	#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
    16	# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
    17	# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
    18	# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
    19	# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
    20	rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
    21	final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
    22	status=0
    23	
    24	while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
    25	  case "$remote_ref" in
    26	    refs/tags/v*)
    27	      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
    28	      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
    29	        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
    30	        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
    31	        status=1
    32	      fi
    33	      ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done
    36	
    37	exit $status

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Runs the BrowserStack Automate suite scoped to one Jira story, the same
     3	# way e2e-browserstack does on a PR — lets a developer execute their
     4	# feature-branch story locally before pushing, using real BrowserStack
     5	# (see .claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping).
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   npm run test:story                  # auto-detects the Jira key(s)
     9	#   npm run test:story -- SFCC-142      # explicit key(s), space-separated
    10	#
    11	# Auto-detection scans commit messages on this branch (commits ahead of
    12	# origin/develop) and the branch name for SFCC-NNN — the same SFCC-[0-9]+
    13	# pattern qa.yml's "Detect Jira story keys" step uses for a PR's title/body/
    14	# branch. Kept as a literal duplicate there rather than a shared script:
    15	# it's one regex, and the input sources genuinely differ (PR text vs local
    16	# git state) — update both if the Jira project key prefix ever changes.
    17	#
    18	# Exit code: 0 if BrowserStack ran (regardless of test pass/fail — that's
    19	# BrowserStack's own exit code), 1 if no Jira key was found or a required
    20	# env var is missing.
    21	
    22	set -euo pipefail
    23	
    24	ENV_FILE=".env"
    25	
    26	if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
    27	    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    28	    set -a && source "$ENV_FILE" && set +a
    29	fi
    30	
    31	KEYS="$*"
    32	
    33	if [[ -z "$KEYS" ]]; then
    34	    BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/develop 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    35	    if [[ -n "$BASE" ]]; then
    36	        COMMIT_MSGS=$(git log "$BASE"..HEAD --pretty=%B 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    37	    else
    38	        COMMIT_MSGS=""
    39	    fi
    40	    BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
    41	    # grep exits 1 on no match, which would otherwise abort the script here
    42	    # under set -e/pipefail before the "no key found" message below can run.
    43	    KEYS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$COMMIT_MSGS" "$BRANCH" | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' || true)
    44	fi
    45	
    46	KEYS=$(echo "$KEYS" | xargs -n1 | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
    47	
    48	if [[ -z "$KEYS" ]]; then
    49	    echo "No Jira story key found." >&2
    50	    echo "Pass one explicitly: npm run test:story -- SFCC-142" >&2
    51	    echo "(auto-detection looks for SFCC-NNN in commit messages on this branch and the branch name)" >&2
    52	    exit 1
    53	fi
    54	
    55	MISSING=()
    56	for var in BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY RETAIL_APP_HOME PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD; do
    57	    if [[ -z "${!var:-}" ]]; then
    58	        MISSING+=("$var")
    59	    fi
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    63	    echo "Missing required env var(s): ${MISSING[*]}" >&2
    64	    echo "Set these in .env — see .env.sample for the full list this needs." >&2
    65	    exit 1
    66	fi
    67	
    68	GREP=$(echo "$KEYS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/@/' | paste -sd '|')
    69	
    70	echo "Running BrowserStack for: $KEYS (--grep \"$GREP\")"
    71	
    72	export SPRINT_NUMBER="${SPRINT_NUMBER:-local-$(whoami)-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)}"
    73	export SITE_ID="${SITE_ID:-au}"
    74	
    75	npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "$GREP"

### Gates that can silently pass having run ZERO items

1. **`npm test` (vitest)** — `passWithNoTests: true` at `vitest.config.ts:12`. If `overrides/` contains no `*.test.ts(x)` files, vitest exits 0 with no output indicating a problem.

2. **`storybook-test` CI job** — if no `*.stories.*` files exist under `overrides/`, `storybook build` produces an empty static site and `test-storybook --ci` visits zero stories, exits 0. No `passWithNoTests: false` equivalent is configured.

3. **`e2e-localhost` CI job with a scoped `--grep`** — when `e2e_scope` is `homepage` (or any other area), the Playwright command is `playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile-chrome --grep "@homepage"`. If no spec carries that Playwright tag, Playwright exits 0 with "0 passed" rather than 1. Mechanism: Playwright's `--grep` filter is a no-match-is-ok operation (`playwright.config.js` has no `reporter`-level failure on zero). (`qa.yml:383`)

4. **`unit-tests`, `storybook-test`, `e2e-localhost`, `e2e-browserstack` CI jobs** — each has an `if:` condition based on `detect-changes` outputs. A job that evaluates to skipped is treated by GitHub as a passing required check (per `qa.yml:14–24` comment). Entire suites can be absent from a PR's check run with a green merge button.
